MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  WORK SESSION
  SPECIAL MEETING
  APRIL 10, 2025
  MULTI-PURPOSE ROOM
  3:00 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 3:04 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne  Riggins;  and
  Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Joseph Toney, Assistant City
  Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Yolanda
  Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director; Maureen Tamuri, Interim Planning
  Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Lauren Doyle, Contract Geologist; Andre
  Ketchedjian, Senior Plan Check Engineer; Michael Phipps, Contract Geologist; and Farah
  Stack, Environmental Sustainability Analyst

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettij ohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on April
  8, 2025.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Riggins seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 1  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Fire Rebuild Policy Discussion
  Recommended Action: Provide direction to the City Manager on key fire recovery
  items described in this report.

  Councilmember Uhring discussed the Archistar AI permit review system.

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Brian Merrick, Reg Brown, Joan Solozki, Jake Holt, Christopher
  Sorenson, Don Schmitz, Darren Graves, Andrew Sheldon, Salwa Wahba, Howard
  Rudzki, Arnold Bernstein, Meghan, Rob, Marissa Coughlan, and Ed Niles
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of April 10, 2025
  Page 2 of 3

  Councilmember Conrad left the dais at 3:54 pm.

  The Council discussed the structure and time limits for meeting.

  Councilmember Conrad returned to the dais 3:56 pm.

  Public Works Director DuBoux discussed and answered questions regarding
  wastewater treatment facilities, the existing Civic Center Water Treatment Facility
  (CCWTF), what would be needed to build a new water treatment facility, other
  possible facilities that could accept the wastewater, remaining capacity in the
  CCWTF, and existing plans for CCWTF Phase 2 and 3. He explained the flve
  options for wastewater treatment for homes in the burn area: 1. Add capacity to the
  CCWTF, 2. Connect to the Hyperion Water Reclamation Plant, 3. Connect to the
  Las Virgenes Municipal Water District, 4. Construct a new water treatment facility,
  and 5. Replace the onsite wastewater treatment systems.

  The Council discussed options for wastewater treatment in the burn area and
  additional information needed to make a final decision.

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, Public Works Director DuBoux stated the
  regional water quality control board would need to agree to changing the scope of
  CCWTF Phase 2 and 3, but there were factors in the City’s favor.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Interim City Attorney Rusin explained
  zoning limits on development.

  The Council further discussed options for wastewater treatment in the burn area.
  They discussed potential alternative funding sources, including State funding, for
  sewer or septic systems and seawalls. The Council expressed interest in receiving
  more information on the cost of a sewer system versus onsite wastewater treatment
  systems and the timeline and challenges for a sewer proj ect. The Council discussed
  which of the flve options should be investigated further and the region that should
  be served by a potential sewer system.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item with more
  information on the five options for wastewater treatment beachfront properties in
  the burn area, including expenses, possible funding sources, timeline and potential
  challenges for each project.

  The Council heard and discussed questions and comments from the public
  regarding: costs and capacity of a sewer system, consultants to manage the sewer
  plan, expense of onsite wastewater treatment systems and seawalls, timeline for
  construction, impacts of seawalls on sandy beaches, temporary use of existing
  onsite wastewater treatment systems while the sewer is developed, seawalls,
  working the State of California, which properties will be served by the sewer, and
  seawalls and coastal erosion.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes ofApril 10, 2025
  Page 3 0f3

  Environmental Sustainability Director Bundy provided information from the
  regional board on requirement for advanced onsite wastewater treatments systems
  for fire rebuilds.

  The Council and the public discussed requirements for onsite wastewater
  treatments systems.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item to consider
  contacting the Governor’s office to request an exemption from requirements to
  build a new advanced onsite wastewater treatment system for fire rebuilds.

RECESS  At 5:40 p.m.. Mayor Stewart recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 5:51
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.

  Mayor Stewart explained that the Work Session needed to be adjourned before 6:00
  p.m. and there was a Closed Session scheduled for 6:00 p.m.

ADJOURNMENT

  At 5:53 p.m., Councilmember Conrad moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Riggins seconded a
  motion to adjourn the meeting to April 24, 2025 at 3:00 p.m. in multi-purpose room. The
  motion carried unanimously.

  Approved and adopted by the City Council of the
  City ofMalibu on August 25, 2025.
